label: rem:cosmological-chirality-flip
title: Chirality reversal at cosmological extremes
html:
The time reversal barrier dictates infinite energy for chirality reversal in the observable sector. The cosmological limits specify two regimes lacking this topological protection.

At the Big Bang (q \to \infty).

The Frobenius form degenerates: \int_A(f^\dagger f) \sim q^{-1} \to 0. The Heisenberg commutator [\hat{X}, \hat{P}]_q \to J is maximal. Observables become maximally non-commutative. The positive-definiteness axiom vanishes.

Here, q acquires an imaginary part \theta \neq 0. The complex substrate interpretation allows continuous fiber chirality rotation. The exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_p supports phase rotation \mathcal{X}_\varphi between trefoils and their mirrors. Chirality flips occur in the fibers.

This meets Sakharov's conditions:

  1. Frobenius degeneration enables baryon number violation.
  2. The deformation magnitude r = \lvert q\rvert supplies CP violation. Not the phase: the framework's matter-antimatter discriminant is \delta_{\mathrm{CP}} = (r^2-1)/(r^2+1) for every \theta (QOU.Observations.crossingDisc_norm_theta_free, sorry-free), so \theta is absent from it — see CP violation evidence. In this regime that strengthens the condition rather than weakening it: as q \to \infty the discriminant tends to 1, its maximum, whereas the phase-based reading would have needed an imperfect projection to leave a residual \theta_{\mathrm{res}}.
  3. The Big Bang provides non-equilibrium.

Condition 2 being satisfied maximally does not close baryogenesis; it sharpens what remains. The framework's asymmetry at the substrate anchor already exceeds the observed baryon-to-photon ratio by \approx 1.7\times10^{8}, so the open object is a suppression, not a further source of asymmetry (again CP violation evidence).

At heat death (q \to 1).

The Hopf algebra becomes cocommutative. The quantum Planck constant vanishes. The Descartes color tubes collapse to a single \mathrm{U}(1) phase tube (prop:u1-equivariant-reduction). The crossing-energy asymmetry q - q^{-1} \to 0 disappears. The electron and muon survive as indistinguishable topological excitations (rem:symmetry-preserving-leptons) with vanishing masses.

Categorical picture (conjectural).

We require a category of QOU degenerations \mathbf{QOU}_{\mathrm{deg}} with morphisms preserving structure while selectively degrading axioms:

  • The initial object represents the Big Bang (q = \infty, degenerate Frobenius form).
  • The terminal object is Bring's surface (q = 1).
  • The observable era is the full subcategory with 1 < q < \infty.

The aeon boundary.

The 1 < q < \infty regime enforces chirality conservation:

  1. Big Bang: Frobenius degeneration lifts the observability constraint. Chirality flips occur freely.
  2. Observable era: Chirality is frozen.
  3. Heat death: The q \to 1 limit erases chirality distinctions.

In a cyclic universe, exceptional divisors reset topology at the aeon boundary. We conjecture this transition as a morphism from the terminal object of one \mathbf{QOU}_{\mathrm{deg}} to the initial object of the next.
